title: Reservoir Weight Allocator and KV Probing Prewarm for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: implement a reservoir-based weight residency allocator plus lightweight KV fingerprint probing that reduces cold-start tails for Dedicated capacity while preserving throughput guarantees and autoscaling safety.

Summary of approach: introduce a probabilistic 'reservoir' budget per fleet that continuously leases GPU memory for model weight residency across tenants. The allocator favors recently used models and tenants with throughput guarantees but includes a small stochastic eviction component to avoid pathological lock-in. In parallel, a low-bandwidth KV probing agent will issue short prefix probes using non-blocking inference micro-requests to hydrate KV caches (and warm tensor shards) for models expected to be invoked by upcoming traffic windows. The two systems coordinate via an admission controller that respects throughput SLO tokens and a burst budget to limit background activity during peak load.

Why different from existing prewarm work: instead of deterministic pinning or simple LRU-based prefetch, reservoir introduces adjustable probabilistic residency with hysteresis and tenant weightings; KV probing uses fingerprint-based selection and micro-probes that avoid full weight loads when possible. This aims to reduce cold-start P95/P99 by targeting likely access paths while keeping background memory/IO within capacity commitments.
acceptance_criteria: P95 cold-start latency improvement >= 30% for label 'interactive' workloads in dedicated fleets compared to baseline (runtime-1.18) as measured on perf dashboard
Background prewarm CPU/GPU utilization increase <= 6% during steady state; IO bandwidth for prewarm <= 12% of allowed burst quota
No regressions in throughput guarantees: dedicated per-tenant throughput measured at 99th percentile remains within SLA of +/-5% under synthetic traffic
Canary rollout plan documented and automated (0%, 1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with automatic rollback on increased error rate or latency regressions
comments: 2026-02-16 - Asha: Spiked initial allocator sketch. Reservoir budget will be represented as a token-bucket style pool per fleet; token cost for residency = memory footprint * residency_priority. Shared doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Reservoir+Allocator+Design
2026-02-20 - Liam: Implemented allocator prototype in rust-service, added in-memory simulator for eviction behavior. Observed steady-state churn decreases vs LRU in simulator for mixed tenant traces.

2026-02-28 - Eng review: Raised two concerns - (1) fairness when one tenant holds many 'hot' models; (2) interaction with autoscaler admission when probes coincide with scale-up. Decided to add a soft cap per-tenant and a probe backoff when scale-up signals detected (PRD updated).

2026-03-03 - Design feedback (Maya, Product): Proposed tenant-weight overrides for customers with throughput-guarantees and a visibility UI in Console (per-tenant warm-score). Added as follow-up in PM backlog.

2026-03-05 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1234 - reservoir allocator and probe scheduler. Includes metrics: reservoir_allocations_total, kv_probe_success_ratio, probe_bytes_used. Pending integration tests.

2026-03-08 - QA: Integration test failures under synthetic peak where probes contributed to a small latency bump. Mitigation: throttle probe rate on autoscaler spike and add probe admission tokens tied to fleet spare capacity metric.

2026-03-10 - Performance: Datadog dashboard snapshot: https://app.datadog.com/dashboard/redwood/reservoir-probe-spike shows P95 cold-start down 34% on canary run with 5% traffic. Next: expand canary and verify long-tail stability.
implementation_notes: Allocator: implement as a separate resident-service with a gRPC control plane to runtime nodes. Residency decisions are cached locally for low-latency checks.
Probe scheduler: server-side agent with three levels - rapid micro-probes (prefix-only, <= 4 tokens), bulk KV warms (when spare capacity present), and deferred bulk pulls during off-peak windows.
Autoscaling integration: admission controller exposes a 'spare_capacity_score' metric; probes are allowed only when score > 0.2 or via explicit admin override.
Telemetry: emit per-tenant reservoir_holders, eviction_reasons (probabilistic|pressure|manual), probe_latency_ms, probe_success_bool; wire to Console for troubleshooting.
Rollout: feature flag gated per-fleet; start with internal fleets and a small set of customers on Dedicated. Use canary progression and automated rollbacks on SLI degradation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Background prewarm could compete with real traffic and increase P50/P95 latency. Mitigation: tokenized admission tied to autoscaler spare capacity and strict burst budgets; default backoff on sustained queueing.

Risk: Reservoir probabilistic eviction might evict a model that immediately becomes hot leading to repeated churn. Mitigation: hysteresis windows and short-term 'sticky' leases for models that have been accessed within last N minutes.
Risk: Cross-tenant fairness issues if high-paying tenant monopolizes residency. Mitigation: tenant soft-caps, weight multipliers based on SLA, and visibility in Console for ops.
Risk: Operational complexity and debugging difficulty. Mitigation: comprehensive telemetry, admin actions (pin/unpin), and detailed runbook for incident response.
